bullets.title: FOMC Debut Under Warsh: Markets Price One Hike by Jan 2027
bullets.body: With new Fed Chair Warsh presiding over his first FOMC meeting June 17, options markets are pricing 88bps moves vs. a 66bps historical average, and futures show ~1 full hike by January 2027. Multiple houses (Goldman, JPMorgan) expect the June dot plot to show no 2026 cuts and possibly signal a 2026-early 2027 hiking sequence as core PCE forecasts move from 2.7% to at least 3.1-3.2%. The Fed is widely expected to remove its easing bias from the statement—characterized as a hawkish move even without a rate change.

bullets.title: May CPI Headline Hot (4.2% YoY), Core Softer (0.2% MoM) — Split Tape
bullets.body: May CPI headline rose 0.47% MoM (+4.2% YoY), highest since April 2023, driven entirely by energy (+3.9% MoM) which accounted for >60% of the monthly gain. Core came in at 0.21% MoM vs. 0.3% expected—the softer print driven by the largest MoM car insurance drop since COVID (-1.7%) and weak core goods. Core PCE nowcasts were revised up to 0.33-0.39% MoM on Thursday's hot PPI (headline +1.1% vs. 0.7% est.; final demand goods +2.8%, largest monthly jump on record). The Fed is expected to mechanically raise its 2026 core PCE forecast to at least 3.2%.

bullets.title: ECB Hikes 25bps — First Since 2023, Signals More Possible
bullets.body: The ECB raised all key rates 25bps (deposit to 2.25%) unanimously, the first hike since 2023, citing Iran war energy spillovers and broadening inflation. Staff projections raised 2026 core inflation to 2.5% from 2.3% and 2027 to 2.5% from 2.2%; GDP growth cut to 0.8% from 0.9% for 2026. Officials cited upside inflation risks and flagged July as a live meeting contingent on energy data. JPMorgan expects one final hike in September but risks skewed to three total.

bullets.title: Iran Deal Inches Closer, Strait Dynamics Remain Fluid
bullets.body: US-Iran tensions remained the dominant macro swing factor. On June 13, Trump announced the deal would be signed 'Sunday' with the Strait of Hormuz opening immediately after; Iran simultaneously signaled the MOU was not a final agreement and that nuclear talks would occur within 60 days. Polymarket priced an 83% chance of a permanent ceasefire by year-end. Wolfe DC Policy cautioned that an MOU remains distant and the most likely forcing mechanism for progress is a negative Treasury/oil market catalyst. Oil fell sharply on deal optimism (WTI -6% on week, below $90 briefly) but reversed on renewed strikes.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler Capex Not Slowing—$670B+ in 2026 and Rising
bullets.body: US hyperscalers (GOOGL, AMZN, META, MSFT) guided capex spend to nearly $800B collectively, with JPMorgan modeling 2027 capex of $1.1-1.4T (vs. consensus $920B). GOOGL raised $80B in equity last week; AMZN secured a $17.5B delayed draw term loan; ORCL raised $40B in FY27. Anthropic secured $35B from BX/APO/AVGO for a 20GW AI XPV platform. AI-related debt issuance surged 47% YTD vs all of 2024 ($159B in first 5 months). GS notes hyperscaler leverage doubled to 1.8x (from 0.9x a year ago) and warns of credit quality drift from AA toward A.

bullets.title: AI Momentum Unwind: Tech -10% in a Week, Rotation into Small Caps
bullets.body: The S&P 500 gained only +0.6% on the week while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell on renewed concerns about AI ROI and CPO delays. Small caps (IWM +4%) and equal-weight S&P outperformed dramatically—the Mag7 underperformed equal-weight NDX by 480bps. Jefferies noted AI drove ~80% of S&P gains in 1Q26 on 39% EPS CAGR but the current correction reflects momentum unwind in crowded AI trades; near-term leadership expected to broaden toward value and yield. Goldman's 1-Delta desk flagged AI infrastructure stock median P/E at 26x (highest since ChatGPT launch) with return dispersion at post-ChatGPT highs.

bullets.title: 10yr Yields Revisit 4.7% Target Amid Hot PPI; Bond Vol Elevated
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised its YE26 2-year target to 4.20% and 10-year to 4.70%, revised higher from 3.90%/4.50%. Rate vol correlation to credit spreads has increased to 0.82 from 0.65. Goldman's fixed income tech desk recommends 10s/30s flatteners as the soft bearish trade. 22V Research notes that 10yr yields above 4.5% historically create demand destruction risk for Early Cyclicals and Tech. Financial conditions remain near historic easy levels (93rd percentile) despite the rate repricing, creating VAR shock risk.

bullets.title: Memory Supercycle Deepens: DRAM/NAND Prices Surge, Supply Locked Through 2028
bullets.body: DRAM ASPs rose mid-60s% QoQ in FY2Q26 and NAND high-70s%; Wolfe raised its FY27 MU EPS forecast to $125 (vs. $107 Street). CSP leaders locked up 2027 capacity and are now moving early to secure 2028 supply—Wolfe projects the shortage persists into CY27/28. SK Hynix completed 375-layer 3D NAND verification and plans mass production by year-end using molybdenum wordlines. NVDA confirmed HBM4 qualification with SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron for Vera Rubin. PC notebook shipments missed expectations in May due to CPU/memory shortages and price increases.

bullets.title: SpaceX IPO: 4x Oversubscribed at $75B Raise, $1.8T Valuation
bullets.body: SpaceX raised $75B in the largest IPO in US history, 4x oversubscribed, with BlackRock ordering $5B+ and Gulf sovereign wealth funds placing $1-5B each. Nasdaq quoted shares at 9:50am June 12, opening around $135 and trading up ~30-35% by close. Wolfe initiated at Outperform $175 PT on Starship reusability thesis and $90B Starlink EBITDA target by 2030. ARK revised its Starlink TAM to $1.6T. Two 2x leveraged ETFs ($SPCH and $SSPC) launched on Monday. North Carolina's treasurer rejected the SpaceX valuation as excessive; Senator Warren requested SEC review.

bullets.title: Anthropic Fable 5/Mythos 5 Launch Triggers AI Export Control Debate
bullets.body: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5 (generally available) and Mythos 5 (restricted to select cyberdefenders), but the US government subsequently ordered Anthropic to block all foreign nationals from accessing these models on national security grounds. Amazon CEO's discussions with Trump administration officials reportedly triggered the crackdown. Microsoft restricted internal employee access to Claude Fable citing data retention concerns. The broader takeaway: AI model-layer regulation is shifting from application to model level, and export controls on frontier AI are now a real policy tool. Anthropic suspended its Mythos model access for foreign nationals.

bullets.title: ORACLE Beats but $70B Capex Guides Disappoint; EPS Upside Delayed
bullets.body: ORCL reported Q4 EPS $2.11 vs $1.96 consensus; revenue $19.18B in-line. RPO surged to $638B (+363% YoY) with $75B from prepaid/customer-supplied GPU contracts. FY27 EPS guide $8.05 (flat) disappointed—gross margins will decline as data centers ramp, but recover over time. Capex guided $90-95B reported ($70B net cash). ORCL plans to raise $40B in FY27 ($20B ATM equity, $20B debt). Stock fell 8-11% post-earnings; sell-side maintained mostly bullish stances on backlog/IaaS momentum. OCI targeted >1GW capacity in Q1 FY27.

bullets.title: AI Token Pricing Under Pressure; OpenAI Considers Drastic Cuts
bullets.body: The SiliconData LLM Token Expenditure Index dropped 6 consecutive days to mid-January levels as enterprises implement 'token budgeting' and shift to cheaper models. OpenAI reportedly considered significant price reductions to compete with Anthropic; Altman told staff an IPO was coming 'within the next year.' Enterprise pushback on AI costs is real—enterprise token rationing reported at WMT, UBER, MSFT. Multiple strategists noted token price compression vs. physical-layer inflation creates a core tension for the AI buildout trade.

bullets.title: CPO Delay Concerns Whipsaw Optical Stocks Before Partial Recovery
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis published research indicating TSMC pushed CPO's OIO tech for GPU-GPU direct connect (scale-up) to 2030-31 due to interposer overheating concerns. This caused a -15-20% selloff in LITE, COHR, AAOI, CIEN, and VIAV. Counter-research from FundAI and Morgan Stanley noted NVDA senior VP denied any delay to CPO ramp, with scale-out CPO ramping late 2026. LITE CEO confirmed at Mizuho conference that company is on pace to meet/exceed top-end of guidance; NPO opportunity described as potentially 'bigger than CPO.' Stocks partially recovered.

bullets.title: US-China Semiconductor Export Controls Tighten Further
bullets.body: Taiwan is weighing stricter AI chip export curbs to China aligned with US restrictions. US lawmakers are pushing for rules restricting contract chipmakers supplying Chinese firms' overseas units. Japan's WF6 supply chain was disrupted by Chinese export controls, threatening ~25% of global supply for SK Hynix, Samsung, and TSM. US officials visited China multiple times to pressure for InP export approval resolution. China's aggregate financing beat in May, suggesting domestic AI capex is accelerating independently.

bullets.title: BOJ Governor Hospitalized, June Rate Hike Still Expected
bullets.body: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda was hospitalized and confirmed to miss the June 16 monetary policy meeting. The June hike to 1.0% is still widely expected per Nikkei reporting. PSC Macro notes the BOJ is behind the curve—Japan's policy rate remains the lowest in developed markets despite nominal GDP growth well above the policy rate.

bullets.title: Market Breadth Broadening; Small Caps and Non-AI Cyclicals Benefiting
bullets.body: 22V Research argues a benign slowdown scenario from ~3% to ~2% GDP growth is positive for Non-AI Cyclicals (Retail, Regional Banks, Airlines, Homebuilders) if 10yr yields stay 4.2-4.5%. Russell 2000 hit new ATH during the week; equal-weighted S&P outperformed cap-weighted by ~120bps. JPM data shows hedge funds reduced Growth exposure for 9 of 12 past weeks and Info Tech exposure in 7 of 12 weeks. 22V's long conviction: Russell 2000 targeting 3,200 (2x S&P YTD).

bullets.title: Prediction Markets Reach $25B Monthly Volume; DKNG Gaining Share
bullets.body: Kalshi's weekly sports handle reached new records, with DKNG disclosing May annualized prediction market volumes of $3.1B (+34% MoM). DKNG CEO confirmed no material cannibalization of OSB and expects the business to be best-in-class by NFL season. Wells Fargo raised 2028+ estimates for DKNG. Regulatory clarity from CFTC's proposed expansive new prediction market rules (allowing most sports bets) was also a positive.

bullets.title: ADBE Q2 Beats But Organic ARR Decelerates; CFO Departs
bullets.body: Adobe reported Q2 revenue $6.62B (+2.6% beat), raised FY26 guide, but cut organic ARR growth guidance by ~$480M (to ~8.6%) due to aggressive freemium pivot delaying monetization. CFO Dan Durn departed to Marvell; CEO search ongoing. Sell-side widely cut PTs 10-15%, Wolfe downgraded to Peer Perform, Evercore to In-Line, Stifel to Hold. The freemium pivot and consecutive C-suite departures signal accelerating competitive disruption risk. NTM P/E compressed to ~8-9x, far below the 24-26x historical average.
